Finding information about an inmate in Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania can be challenging, but the county provides multiple official resources to help you locate someone in the correctional system. Whether you're searching for a family member, friend, or need to verify custody status, this guide walks you through the philadelphia county pennsylvania inmate lookup process and connects you with official government resources. Learn how to search jail records, understand visitation policies, and get answers to common questions about the Philadelphia County jail system.

How to Search Philadelphia County Jail Records

  1. Visit the Philadelphia County Official Inmate Search — Go to the Philadelphia Department of Prisons inmate locator at prison.phila.gov. This is the fastest way to search current inmates held in Philadelphia County facilities.
  2. Enter the Inmate's Name or ID Number — Type the full name (or partial name) and any known identification number. The system will display matching results with custody status and current housing assignments.
  3. Check the Pennsylvania Department of Corrections Database — If the person is not in county custody, they may have been transferred to state prison. Search the PA DOC inmate locator at www.cor.pa.gov to check state facilities.
  4. Verify Court Records for Pending Cases — Visit the Philadelphia County Courts website to search for active cases, charges, bail amounts, and scheduled court dates. This helps you understand the legal status and timeline.
  5. Contact the Department Directly if Search Results Are Unclear — Call the Philadelphia Department of Prisons main line or visit in person if the online search doesn't provide the information you need. Staff can confirm custody status and answer specific questions.

Bail Bond Information for Philadelphia County

When someone is arrested in Philadelphia County, bail is typically set during the arraignment hearing, which usually occurs within 72 hours of arrest. Bail can be paid directly to the court, or you can hire a bail bondsman to post bail on your behalf. A licensed bail bondsman typically charges a non-refundable fee of 10 percent of the total bail amount set by the judge. For example, if bail is set at $10,000, the bondsman fee would be $1,000. This fee is the cost of their service and is kept by the bonding company regardless of whether the defendant appears in court.

The bail process in Philadelphia County moves quickly once the bail amount is posted. If bail is paid directly to the court, the inmate is usually released within a few hours. If using a bail bond company, the process may take slightly longer as the bonding company must post the bond with the court before release. It's important to contact a bail bondsman immediately after arrest if you cannot afford the full bail amount out of pocket. Many bail bond companies in the Philadelphia area offer 24/7 service and can post bonds quickly to get your loved one released as soon as possible.

Visitation Rules at Philadelphia County Jail

  • Identification Required — Visitors must present a valid government-issued photo ID (driver's license, passport, or state ID). Children must be accompanied by an adult who can provide identification for both.
  • Visiting Hours — Philadelphia County Department of Prisons typically allows visits during specific hours on weekends and certain weekday evenings. Call ahead to confirm current visitation schedules, as hours may vary by facility.
  • Dress Code — Visitors must dress appropriately. No revealing clothing, tank tops, or clothing with logos is permitted. Comfortable, modest clothing is recommended.
  • Video Visitation Available — If in-person visits are not possible, the Philadelphia County system offers video visitation through an approved vendor. This allows remote contact with inmates from home or a designated location.
  • Children's Visitation Policy — Children may visit inmates but must follow all facility rules and be supervised by a responsible adult at all times. Infants are generally permitted, but policies may restrict visits by very young children during certain hours.

What to Expect After Arrest in Philadelphia County

  1. Booking Process — Upon arrest, the inmate is brought to a Philadelphia County processing facility where personal information, charges, and identifying details are recorded. This step takes 1–2 hours and includes fingerprinting and photography.
  2. Medical Screening — A medical evaluation is performed to assess the inmate's health status and identify any immediate medical needs or infectious disease concerns. Mental health screening also occurs during this phase.
  3. Classification Assessment — Staff determine the inmate's security level based on criminal history, charges, and behavior. This affects housing assignment and program eligibility throughout the stay.
  4. Arraignment Hearing — Usually within 72 hours, the inmate appears before a judge for arraignment where charges are read, bail is set, and the inmate is informed of their rights. This hearing is critical for bail determination.
  5. Housing Assignment or Transfer — After arraignment, the inmate is assigned to a housing unit based on classification level, or transferred to another facility if the case is disposed of or bail is paid. The inmate may also be transferred to state custody if convicted of a felony with a sentence exceeding one year.

Frequently Asked Questions — Philadelphia County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Philadelphia County jail?

Use the Philadelphia County Department of Prisons inmate search tool at prison.phila.gov/inmate-locator/. Enter the person's first and last name (or partial name) to see if they are currently in custody. You can also call the Department of Prisons main line to verify custody status by phone. If the person is not found in the county system, check the Pennsylvania Department of Corrections database to see if they were transferred to state prison.

How long does booking take in Philadelphia County?

The booking process in Philadelphia County typically takes 1–2 hours from the time of arrival at the facility. This includes intake processing, fingerprinting, photography, medical screening, and classification assessment. After booking is complete, the inmate is held until their arraignment hearing, which must occur within 72 hours of arrest. Keep in mind that wait times may vary depending on facility volume and complexity of charges.

Can I visit an inmate at Philadelphia County jail?

Yes, visitation is permitted at Philadelphia County facilities during designated hours. Visitors must be at least 18 years old (younger visitors need a responsible adult), present a valid photo ID, and follow dress code rules. In-person visiting hours typically occur on weekends and select weekday evenings, though schedules vary by facility. If in-person visits are inconvenient, you can arrange video visitation through the county's approved vendor from a computer or phone.

What if the person is not in the county jail system?

If your search in the Philadelphia County system returns no results, the person may have been transferred to another facility or released. Check the Pennsylvania Department of Corrections inmate locator at www.cor.pa.gov to see if they are in a state prison facility. You can also search the Federal Bureau of Prisons database at www.bop.gov/inmateloc/ if federal charges are involved. If still not found, contact the Philadelphia County Courts to verify whether charges were dropped or the person was released on bail.

How do I send money to an inmate in Philadelphia County?

Commissary deposits can be made through the Philadelphia County Department of Prisons' approved vendor. Most facilities offer online deposit options, phone payments, and in-person payments at designated locations. Visit the Department of Prisons website or call their main line for current commissary deposit methods, accepted payment types, and any fees that may apply. Money deposited goes into the inmate's account to purchase items from the prison commissary such as toiletries, snacks, and clothing.
